output.reason: A 28-year-old with 2 days of dysuria and increased urinary frequency, no reported fever or back pain and not pregnant, has a likely uncomplicated lower UTI needing clinician assessment and possible antibiotic prescribing, which can safely start in messaging.
output.patientMessage: Send this to a Counsel clinician in this thread today for review; burning and frequent urination for two days most often means a bladder infection, which usually needs assessment and possibly antibiotics. Drink fluids meanwhile. If you develop fever, chills, back or flank pain, vomiting, or blood in your urine, seek same-day in-person care instead of waiting for a reply.

citations.claim: Complicating factors such as pregnancy, male sex, obstruction or immunosuppression define complicated UTI; none are reported here, supporting non-urgent async review.
citations.limitation: ED reference synthesis listing complicating factors; absence of reported factors does not confirm they are absent.
